text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wedensday:

- Unemployment rate in September rose by 0.1 percentage points to 4.6 percent compared with the previous month, the Federal Office for Statistics reported. Swiss trade unions talk of 'alarming' figures.

- Swiss government on Tuesday decided not to ship 230,000 cows to Nepal. The Nepalese World Hindu Federation said earlier it would offer asylum to the cows, which will be slaughtered in an attempt to eradicate mad cow disease in Switzerland.

- Swiss entrepreneur Georg Endress plans to build what he calls a 'Biovalley' in the region of Basle and the neighbouring regions in Germany and France. On Tuesday, scientists, business representatives and politicians discussed the feasibility of this project in the French town of Colmar.

- Major cantonal banks lowered the mortgage rate by a quarter percentage point to 4.75 percent. Rents are expected to fall. - Swiss hearing aid producer Phonak will take over Norwegian competitor E. Stephensen AS.
- The number of vacant flats in Switzerland rose to 1.61 percent in June.

- French-speaking town Neuchatel allocated a 5.2 million Swiss franc credit for Expo 2001, a major exhibition held in the year 2001. The total costs of Expo 2001 will amount to 1.3 billion Swiss francs.
